w: San Jose's Michelin Bib Gourmand Mexican kitchen on The Alameda: an ingredient-first, from-scratch room (heirloom-corn tortillas, house salsas) that elevates carne asada tacos, esquites and enchiladas without leaving the everyday-taqueria spirit behind. The most decorated Mexican table in the South Bay.
sources: guide.michelin.com — LUNA Mexican Kitchen, Bib Gourmand, San Jose; 1495 The Alameda

address: 1175 E Julian St Ste 5, San Jose, CA 95116
w: A 1982 East-San-Jose taqueria carrying the flavors of Jalisco: spit-roasted al pastor, carne asada and a fast counter line that has anchored the E Julian St / Alum Rock side of town for four decades. A benchmark for the neighborhood taqueria the city is known for.
sources: yelp.com/biz/taqueria-el-grullense-san-jose-3 — open, updated July 2026; 1175 E Julian St, est. 1982

w: A homegrown San Jose mini-chain (this is the original SoFA-adjacent S 10th St location) that locals reach for first — crackly-edged carnitas, reliably hot food and friendly counter service, open till late. Featured by The Infatuation's San Jose guide.
sources: theinfatuation.com/san-jose — named in the Best Restaurants in San Jose guide
yelp.com/biz/super-taqueria-san-jose-2 — open, updated Aug 2026; 480 S 10th St

w: A West San Jose institution whose carnitas — served open-face, juicy inside and crisped at the edges — draw a devoted following; regulars call them among the best in the Bay. Also strong al pastor and quesadillas.
sources: yelp.com/biz/taqueria-eduardo-san-jose-2 — open, updated Aug 2026 (679 reviews); 3123 Williamsburg Dr

w: A The Alameda favorite that hand-presses every tortilla from organic corn masa (La Finca, Oakland) and won a San Jose best-taco award; the fresh-masa tacos and antojitos are the reason. Featured by The Infatuation's San Jose guide.
sources: theinfatuation.com/san-jose — named in the Best Restaurants in San Jose guide
yelp.com/biz/zona-rosa-san-jose — open, updated Aug 2026 (1,771 reviews); 1411 The Alameda

w: A contemporary East-San-Jose Mexican room that feels transplanted from Mexico City or Guadalajara: chile-adobo duck confit under chocolate-chile mole, plus mushroom-and-hibiscus tacos. The city's most ambitious modern-Mexican table. Featured by The Infatuation's San Jose guide.
sources: theinfatuation.com/san-jose — named in the Best Restaurants in San Jose guide as a contemporary Mexican pick
yelp.com/biz/acopio-san-jose — open, updated July 2026; 399 S 24th St

w: A family-run North San Jose taqueria (since 2017) built on Mexico City and Jalisco cooking — al pastor, huaraches, homemade salsas and weekend molcajete with hand-made tortillas. Featured by The Infatuation's San Jose guide.
sources: theinfatuation.com/san-jose — named in the Best Restaurants in San Jose guide

address: 401 S King Rd, San Jose, CA 95116
w: An East San Jose drive-thru taqueria on S King Rd cooking authentic Jalisco-style plates fresh daily, with a window open until 3 a.m. Friday and Saturday — the go-to when the sit-down spots have closed.
sources: yelp.com/biz/jalisco-taqueria-san-jose — open, updated July 2026; 401 S King Rd, late-night drive-thru

w: Willow Glen-edge mariscos done Sinaloa-style: bright, chile-electric aguachile, ceviche and shrimp cocktails from a kitchen that leans on coastal-Mexican technique. Open late on weekends.
sources: yelp.com/biz/camaron-de-sinaloa-san-jose — open, updated July 2026 (490 reviews); 245 Willow St

address: 1805 Alum Rock Ave, San Jose, CA 95116
w: A long-running Alum Rock Ave mariscos house at the heart of East San Jose's Mexican corridor — heaping seafood cocktails, ceviche tostadas and caldos in a bustling neighborhood room.
sources: yelp.com/biz/la-costa-san-jose-2 — open, updated Aug 2026 (1,014 reviews); 1805 Alum Rock Ave

w: A packed North 13th St seafood-Mexican spot beloved for its campechana cocktails, aguachile and whole-fish plates — one of the highest-volume mariscos rooms in the city.
sources: yelp.com/biz/mariscos-costa-alegre-san-jose — open, updated June 2026 (1,148 reviews); 855 N 13th St

dish: build-your-own burrito at the burrito bar
address: 235 E Middlefield Rd Ste 1A, Mountain View, CA 94043
w: A 1984 Mountain View family institution famous for its burrito bar — you walk the line and build a burrito bigger than your head (it once set a Guinness record for the largest burrito). A Silicon Valley rite of passage.
sources: yelp.com/biz/la-costena-mountain-view-5 — open, updated July 2026; 235 E Middlefield Rd, est. 1984

address: 2020 W El Camino Real, Mountain View, CA 94040
w: A Mountain View sit-down Mexican room revered for its moles — enchiladas bathed in a richly spiced, cocoa-deepened sauce — a step up from the taqueria counter for regional dishes and dinner service.
sources: yelp.com/biz/vive-sol-mountain-view — open, updated July 2026 (1,516 reviews); 2020 W El Camino Real

address: 3636 El Camino Real, Palo Alto, CA 94306
w: Palo Alto's top taqueria on El Camino Real — all-day breakfast, al pastor and carne asada tacos and burritos from open till late, the rare no-frills taqueria on the pricey Peninsula stretch.
sources: yelp.com/biz/taqueria-el-grullense-palo-alto — open, updated July 2026 (642 reviews); 3636 El Camino Real

w: A Sunnyvale counter that tops the area's al pastor lists — quick, cheap, spit-roasted pastor tacos and burritos filling the taqueria gap on the north-county side.
sources: yelp.com/biz/speedys-tacos — open, updated 2026; 929 E Duane Ave, Sunnyvale

w: The taqueria counter inside a Mexican supermarket — a South Bay genre unto itself: order carne asada and al pastor tacos off the carnicería, grab pan dulce from the panadería, eat like a local. This is the Sunnyvale/N Fairoaks branch.
sources: yelp.com/biz/chavez-supermarket-and-taqueria-sunnyvale — open, updated Aug 2026 (509 reviews); 666 N Fairoaks Ave

address: 700 S Winchester Blvd Ste 25, San Jose, CA 95128
w: San Jose's go-to Peruvian kitchen near Santana Row: tender beef lomo saltado over fries and rice, plus causa, tiradito and ceviche — the South Bay's most reliable window into Peruvian cooking.
sources: yelp.com/biz/inkas-restaurant-san-jose-2 — open, updated July 2026 (281 reviews); 700 S Winchester Blvd

w: A South San Jose Salvadoran standby for hand-patted pupusas — revueltas and loroco griddled thick and served with curtido and salsa roja — plus tamales and platos típicos.
sources: yelp.com/biz/pupuseria-delmy-san-jose — open, updated April 2026 (146 reviews); 3039 Monterey Rd

address: 1442 S White Rd, San Jose, CA 95127
w: An East San Jose Colombian kitchen for the full bandeja paisa — beans, chicharrón, chorizo, arepa and fried egg on one plate — plus house-made cheese arepas. Fills the South Bay's Colombian gap.
sources: yelp.com/biz/fonda-colombiana-san-jose — open, updated July 2026 (114 reviews); 1442 S White Rd
